clue.text: Equipment includes new telephone

definitions.note: a verb here: to call someone on the phone

indicators.note: includes says the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment, as in a drilling rig

explanation.surface: A new phone comes bundled with some kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'telephone' looks like a noun in the surface, but it is the verb: to give someone a call.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a call is to make their phone sound, so the verb for phoning someone fits.

clue.text: Ratify a fine company

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Someone signs off a company's paperwork for a fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to confirm formally or give official approval to something.

clue.text: Mist surrounds river and pond creature

indicators.note: surrounds says the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: fog is a thick mist
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A misty scene by a river where pond life lurks.
explanation.definitionFit: This amphibian is the classic creature found living in and around garden ponds.

clue.text: Not something you'll salvage from a wreck, perhaps

definitions.text: Not something you'll salvage from a wreck, perhaps

parts.words: Not something you'll salvage from a wreck, perhaps
parts.note: the wreck is a crashed car, not a ship: after an accident claim the motor insurance discount for claim-free years is lost

explanation.surface: Divers or beachcombers picking over a shipwreck for anything worth saving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreck' suggests a ship and 'salvage' treasure; in fact a car crash costs you the insurance discount you had built up.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor insurers give a discount for each year without a claim; a crash and claim usually wipes it out.

clue.text: Alarming changes in key election seat

definitions.note: a noun here: a constituency that could easily change hands

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Worrying shifts in a seat that could decide an election.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a seat held by a slim majority, which could easily be lost, is known by this name and gets most campaign attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituency won by a narrow margin is the battleground where elections are decided, hence key.

clue.text: Job almost entirely involving the mail

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: almost says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all gone

explanation.surface: Someone's work is nearly all about handling letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final L from ALL, leaving AL.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything to do with the post, as in a postal vote or postal service.

clue.text: Instrument, note, used in lively recital

indicators.note: used in says the first piece is placed within the second
lively suggests the letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician plays a note on some instrument during an energetic concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lively' rearranges RECITAL into CLARIET, and 'used in' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This woodwind with a single reed is one of the orchestra's standard instruments.

clue.text: Fire or non-fire, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether something is ablaze or not.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen is ignored: 'possibly' rearranges the seven letters of NONFIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a huge, raging blaze, so it is a fire on a grand scale.

clue.text: String of islands having a charge for crossing?

parts.note: a toll is a fee for using a bridge or road

explanation.surface: A chain of islands that makes visitors pay to go between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A coral reef forms a ring of small islands around a lagoon, so it is a string of islands.

clue.text: Summons to meal draws in one attending

indicators.note: draws in says the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: a gong is struck to call people to dinner
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The dinner gong pulls in a guest at the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one attending' looks like a person; 'one' is I and 'attending' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are going to an event you are attending it: both mean being present there.

clue.text: Boat more likely to float?

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to carry goods to and from ships
having less weight, so likelier to stay up in water

explanation.surface: Asking which boat would stay afloat better.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a barge and is also the comparative of an adjective meaning not heavy.

clue.text: Curious when taken aback by excellent Japanese warrior

indicators.note: taken aback says the words before it are read backwards

parts.note: rum means curious or odd
as means when, as in as I left
A1 means excellent, written AI with the figure taken as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised by an excellent Japanese fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns RUMAS into SAMUR. A1 (first class) is read with the 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: These were the hereditary military class of feudal Japan, sword-carrying fighters.

clue.text: I'm beginning to mature in handling of golf-club under waterlogged conditions

indicators.note: in says the first pieces go inside the next

parts.note: a golfer's swing is how they handle the club

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A young golfer improving their swing on a rain-soaked course.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor or field that is awash, flooded with water, is said to be this, as in a kitchen awash in water.

clue.text: Boy, English, engaged in study? That's sensible

indicators.note: engaged in says the first pieces are held within the next

parts.note: to read is to study a subject at university
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An English lad at his studies asks if that is sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' is the British use of read, as in reading history at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Something logically thought out is sensible, built on sound argument.

clue.text: Manmade material sported by many Londoners

indicators.note: sported by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A synthetic fabric worn by lots of people in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a synthetic polymer fibre, the first fully man-made textile.

clue.text: Country I name that has rejected support

indicators.note: rejected says the word is turned back the other way

parts.note: aid means support or help

explanation.surface: A speaker names a nation that turned down help.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Asian republic is a nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: A mistake to change sides?

definitions.meaning: to desert one's country or party for the opposition

explanation.surface: Wondering whether switching allegiance would be an error.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a flaw or fault; the verb is to abandon one side for its rival.

clue.text: Prominent foreigner seen in street

indicators.note: seen in says the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: A stranger stands out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient features stick out and catch the eye, so they are prominent.

clue.text: Wind up new newspaper appearing in middle of week

indicators.note: appearing in says the first pieces sit within the next
middle of takes the central letters of the word that follows

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging name for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A paper published midweek riles its readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind up' is British slang for annoy, not the end of something; the middle of WEEK is EE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind someone up in British slang is to annoy them, and to infuriate is a stronger form.

clue.text: Gangster in Sofia, corrupt in a short time

indicators.note: in says the first piece goes around the next

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

indicators.note: corrupt says the letters of the word are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A mobster in the Bulgarian capital turns bent overnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sofia' reads as the Bulgarian capital but is only letters; 'corrupt' scrambles them, and 'in' puts MO around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Mafia, the Sicilian-American crime syndicate, is a gangster.

clue.text: Danger for each one left

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A risk that leaves one person behind every time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means serious risk or jeopardy, a straightforward synonym for danger.

clue.text: Compassion? Heartless party will suppress it

indicators.note: will suppress says the first piece holds the second down inside it
heartless removes the middle letters of the next word, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A heartless political party crushes any show of sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: This means sorrow felt for another's suffering, close in sense to compassion.

clue.text: First of lunches consumed behind schedule

indicators.note: First of takes the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: ate means consumed, as food

explanation.surface: Lunch is eaten past the usual time.
explanation.definitionFit: Running behind schedule means arriving after the expected time, which is tardy.

clue.text: Small corner hard to be found in French resort

indicators.note: to be found in says the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tricky little nook somewhere in a Riviera town.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess or nook in a wall is a small corner, often holding an ornament.

clue.text: Out of bed, drunk and tense

parts.note: up means risen from bed
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone up, intoxicated and on edge after a rough night.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone anxious and unable to relax is nervy or on edge, the informal sense here.
